Align gene trees to disk and read selected genes

align_panel_to_disk.Rd

The first pass aligns each batch in a separate R process, writes gene-level evidence to disk and indexes distinct fusion patterns by their original reference branches. In a second pass, readers return the genes and columns requested from the relevant batches. Reference branch identifiers are local to the panel.

Usage

align_panel_to_disk(species_tree, gene_file, output_dir,
  mode = c("free", "fixed", "paired"), fixed_file = NULL, batch_size = 32L,
  fusion_view = c("whole", "direct"))
export_panel_matrix(path, file, component = "free_length", include_fusions = FALSE)
read_panel_fusion_cells(path, genes, patterns, role = "free")
panel_fusion_patterns(path)
read_panel_matrix(path, component, genes, branches = NULL)
read_panel_groups(path, genes, role = "free")
read_panel_fusions(path, genes, patterns, role = "free",
  field = c("numeric_value", "recovery_status"))

Arguments

species_tree

Path to the reference Newick file.

gene_file

Path to a file with one named record such as gene1(A,B); per line. The name follows the SplitAligner file convention (letters, digits, dot, underscore or hyphen). In paired mode, supply the free trees here.

output_dir

A new directory under an existing parent.

mode

Process free trees, fixed trees or paired tree sets.

fixed_file

In paired mode, the matching fixed trees in the same gene order.

batch_size

Positive number of genes per worker process. Reduce for wider reference trees.

path

Path to a completed panel directory. Keep its manifest and batch files together.

genes

Gene IDs or positive integer row positions, in the desired order. For read_panel_fusions() and read_panel_fusion_cells(), an empty character or numeric vector requests zero rows or cells, respectively.

file

A new TSV file under an existing parent directory on a filesystem that supports hard links. Existing paths, including dangling symbolic links, are never replaced.

include_fusions

For length matrices, append one column for each indexed fusion pattern. Groups with no finite length write NA. Use the group reader to inspect the reason.

component

One of free_state, free_length, fixed_state, fixed_length, paired_free or paired_fixed, depending on mode.

branches

Primitive branch IDs or positive column positions. The default includes all primitive branches.

patterns

Composite IDs or positive column positions from panel_fusion_patterns(), in the desired order. For read_panel_fusions() and read_panel_fusion_cells(), an empty character or numeric vector requests zero columns or cells, respectively.

role

Tree set to read, either "free" or "fixed".

fusion_view

Recorded numerical rule for this panel. The default sums recovered whole components with usable lengths. Use "direct" to export only lengths of active groups.

field

Numerical value under the recorded view, or the legacy recovery status of an active group. For recovery of decomposable coordinates use read_panel_fusion_cells().

Details

Every new panel writes support.tsv and support.nwk in its free or fixed subdirectory. Paired panels write both sets. Counts are added across batches before the support percentages are computed. An internal branch with no eligible genes has NA in the table and a blank tree label. Both files are indexed by relative path and SHA-256 in manifest$support. Older panel directories remain readable and can be rebuilt from the original inputs to generate these files.

A fusion pattern can occur on either side of a paired run. Within a gene and role, a pattern that does not form has no sparse group row. In a new whole-view panel the numeric cell can still have a value if complete, recovered branches cover exactly the target members and every branch has a usable length. Source splits, Newick node indices and construction mode are available from read_panel_fusion_cells. Legacy v1 panels retain their original direct-only values. A group that forms has a recovery status of recovered_numeric, recovered_numeric_unavailable or unrecovered. Only free-tree group records use the NA_fuse_topo classification. Primitive and fused lengths are available separately.

Memory scales with batch width, the gene and pattern indexes, and the requested slice. Matrix reads default to a limit of 10 million requested cells. Set the positive option SplitAlignerR.max_panel_cells to change the limit or set it to Inf to remove it. Use tempfile() for an automatically named temporary output directory. Readers verify each requested batch against its stored SHA-256 checksum. A completed panel is marked by manifest.rds. A new run requires a fresh directory. Full in-memory provenance and exchange objects remain available via align_branches.

Value

The writer returns the panel directory. The exporter streams one TSV row per gene and returns the file path. The catalog is a data frame of coordinate_id and primitive_members. Matrix readers return the requested rows and columns in selection order. Empty selections in read_panel_fusions() retain the matrix type and the other axis's names. The group reader returns a data frame with one record per formed group and selected gene. The fusion-cell reader identifies each cell by gene_id and composite_id. Its rows follow the requested pattern order, with the requested gene order within each pattern, matching fusion_cells. Repeated selections repeat their rows. If either selection is empty, it returns the same columns and types with zero rows.
